source_text: So, the work from claude-17 on the daxiang_live.html page seems quite convincing and I don't want to disrupt that just to introduce new blending machinery.  But I think we now have all the formal pieces that we would need to develop a convincing cascade, the various components are all just a bit scattered.  On the one hand there are the experiments that you found that proved that a cascade is more efficient than a flat list.   To my knowledge we haven't proved that it is similarly more efficient than a chain (linear logic) but I think it should be, particularly if we take into account the formation cost.   Let me trot out a conceptual idea that has been on my mind for a while.  Alexander said "a city is not a tree".  I had the riff that "a proof is not a tree".  The reason for this is, the tree presents a *parse* of the proof, but not the proof's formation.  In the same way, we could no doubt turn a cascade into a linear do-this-then-do-this... recipe.  But the recipe is strictly additional work beyond the formation of the cascade which would be via conceptual blending.  Anyway, we have the 3/2 category story, we have the "wants" token story, and we have the recent claude-17 small-causal world story.  What I think we need to do is carefully bring these ingredients together.  Moreover, the other thing we *should* have is ONE cascade from the outer loop that is a policy for selecting META items for the inner loop.  In that case minimizing G *doesn't* mean changing the cascade structurally in the same way would happen in the usual cascade scenario.  Minimizing G in the outer loop is parametric in the selection of META item.  Neverless I'd contend that the outer loop cascade should "look like" a cascade.  So rather than concocting a made up example, I think we should explore that one in a bit more detail.  It might be, for example, that we really do need to change it structurally depending on circumstances.  But this is something to explore.

reply_text:
㊥ (gist) I took the outer-loop cascade as the real example and read it three ways on run c9d25d6a's record. The note is `futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/NOTE-outer-cascade-as-pasted-blends-2026-10-05.md` (futon2 `1f2bd525d`), no code touched and daxiang_live untouched. Short version: the outer cascade already exists as a diamond of four meta patterns whose precedence set *is* a semilattice, the blend reading derives that diamond from what the four patterns share, the token reading makes it the first non-toy `ConstructionReceipt`, and the causal reading shows that the click performed one of its four patterns. Your "parametric in the META item" has a clean statement in Goguen's terms, and so does the circumstance under which structure must change.

㊢ ("ONE cascade from the outer loop") There are two outer loops. `futon3/library/meta/meta-outer-policy-cascade.edn` (2 Oct) is the diamond: observe → {fill, injury} → minimise, four edges, two linear extensions, six typed slots, argmin-G, boundary `:produces :selected-meta-policy`. Its evaluator `meta_outer_policy.clj` is called by nothing in the click. What the click runs is `meta_live_outer_selector` → `meta_pipeline_selector/select` over Cascade Live: on c9d25d6a it excluded 569 of 676 items (506 off the current map), ranked 107 by a pairwise sum of cost channels, and selected `M-interim-director-proxy-metric-inventory` because its centrality cost `1/(1+33)` was lowest; `:epistemic-value-nats 0.0`, no injury observation, no outer-policy receipt. So the META item was chosen by a centrality ranking, not by the cascade.

🈖 ("minimizing G *doesn't* mean changing the cascade structurally") In 3/2 terms: the tactical loop constructs the *diagram* per problem and G orders diagrams; the outer loop fixes the diagram and G orders the *cones* over minimise's square — each filled candidate is a consistent cone over (admitted family, generative model, shared outcome vocabulary), and Goguen's "two different 3/2-pushouts need not be isomorphic" is precisely two META items being different blends of the same inputs. The target slot is the parameter; the squares do not move.

🈖 ("we really do need to change it structurally depending on circumstances") Structure must change exactly when the fixed diagram has no non-degenerate cone: a required slot unfillable from HEAD (the record shows the shape — `declared-priority-cost` filled for 0 of 107, freshness for 79), a singleton family, or injury with no matching A item. In the first case a *reading* square (your 25 Sept read-criteria / ask / defer steps, with epistemic value when the fact is absent) gets pasted in before `fill`. So: four fixed squares plus a fifth under a stated absence, and which absence can be read from the record rather than guessed.

㊢ (bringing the three stories together) Blend: each meta pattern's I₁, I₂, G, B read off its own text (table in §2 of the note); observe's B is an input of both fill and injury, which is why they are incomparable and one frontier, and fill's and injury's Bs are minimise's two inputs, which is why minimise is their meet. Tokens: the same four edges carry `{field-observation}`, `{field-observation, injury-observation}`, `{filled-candidates, typed-exclusions}`, `{admitted-support, rearm-slot}` — the gluing object of the blend reading and the token of the receipt are one thing seen from two sides, which was the bridge v3 §3 left open. Causal: with claude-17's compiler unchanged and link theories running down the diamond instead of up the `@why` cone, the c9d25d6a record reads as observe partly met, fill unmet, injury unobserved, minimise unmet — his §9 item 3 applied to a click.

㊟ ("a cascade is more efficient than a flat list … haven't proved … than a chain") In the code the list and the chain are one object: the list kernel fires one pattern per step in order. So the two measurements we have (30 Sept: chain 3.0749 vs one-edge 1.4147; 5 Oct: list 10.715 vs frontier 9.465) are already cascade-versus-chain, both under a per-step C, neither with formation cost. What is unmeasured is the bag, and there v2's "a missing edge is not simultaneous success" has to enter the score first or the bag wins for free. Formation cost as accounting: forming the chain = forming the cascade + choosing a linear extension, log₂(#extensions) bits (one for the diamond) and no token — that is your "recipe is strictly additional work" and "a proof is not a tree", made countable, not yet measured.

㊭ (next checks, each dispatchable alone, in order) 1. Slot census at HEAD: run `meta_policy_constructor/construct` over the 107 on-map items and tabulate fillable slots — says whether the diamond ever has a non-degenerate cone on today's field and which absence forces the reading square. 2. Lean: the diamond as a `ConstructionReceipt` (four units, one meet witness, `valid = true`) and its two chains with the token-less forged edge, `valid = false`. 3. The per-click unmet table computed from a record with claude-17's `ot/glue`, not by hand. 4. The four-number experiment on the diamond: diamond, two extensions, bag, under construction's per-step C with the ordering term. 5. Only after those: whether the live selector gives way to the diamond-with-reading-square, which is an operating change and yours.

🈸 (go-ahead) Shall I dispatch 1 and 2 now (discovery to a codex seat, the Lean example myself), leaving 3 to claude-17 since it is his compiler? Also unchanged: the two v3 decisions from my last report still await you.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
("Goguen 1-and-a-half categories") The source is Goguen's "An Introduction to Algebraic Semiotics" (1999), Appendix B, now filed with checksums in `wm-contract/refs/`. Its text layer is garbled, so I read the four pages by eye. What it says:
- **A 3/2-category** is a category whose arrows between two objects are partially ordered, by quality: one map is above another when it preserves at least as much content, every axiom the other does, and is as inclusive. He calls them "one and a half" categories in a footnote.
- **A 3/2-pushout** keeps the shape of a pushout but replaces "exactly one mediating map" with "a best one": among the maps from the blend to any other candidate blend, there is a maximum.
- **Non-uniqueness is the point.** "Two different 3/2-pushouts need not be isomorphic; this means that ambiguity is natural in this setting."
- **Pasting holds.** The composition of two 3/2-pushouts is a 3/2-pushout, a 2×2 grid of them is one, and the colimit of any connected diagram can be built from them. One caution: pasting two consistent squares can give an inconsistent figure, so consistency has to be checked.
- **Names matter.** Isomorphic cones do not represent the same blend, because which element goes to which is part of the blend.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("a houseboat and a boathouse") His 2006 paper gives the full example. From house and boat he lists six blends: houseboat, boathouse, a boat that carries houses, an amphibious RV, a livable boat for transporting livable boats, and a boat used on land as a house; the Alloy program found 42 more, "most of which are far from optimal". He also writes that for this example "the most natural blend is an ordinary pushout, all the other good blends are 3/2-pushouts, and various blends that fail to preserve as much structure as they could are not any kind of pushout". Only houseboat has all its triangles commuting; the others have what he calls auxiliary maps.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("emergent structure") Two statements of his, five years apart: in 1999, that the quality order itself "captures what Fauconnier and Turner have called emergent structure, without needing any other machinery"; in 2006, a hypothesis that emergent structure arises by recruiting an extra space that matches concepts the inputs mention but the common ground did not integrate. Read against construction, the second is a rule for where an extension candidate comes from. I put it in the draft as open, not as a rule.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the draft says, in brief)
1. The unit is a square: two inputs, what they share, and the blend, each recorded as text with its source, supplied by a reading of the pattern for the problem. No slot mapping, on the evidence of the sample.
2. v2's three relations are derived: support is a leg into a blend; a meet is the shared object under two occurrences, named as text and required only where two occurrences are glued; precedence is two orders kept apart, construction order forced and application order evidenced. v2's rule against simultaneity from a missing edge stands.
3. Occurrences that share nothing are a bag, reported as such. The last click's cascade is a bag by this rule.
4. Same inputs with different maps are different policies, which is your requirement Q10 in Goguen's words.
5. Five added Lean obligations, including finite witnesses of non-uniqueness and of inconsistent pasting.
6. Left open: how the quality order enters G; the relation to the existing co-application kernel; which parts of a library pattern are the inputs.
